correctness.rationale: Every nonzero hollow symmetric projective matrix has an invertible off-diagonal two-by-two pivot. Elementary invertible row/column operations identify the localized 3-minor ideal exactly with the Schur complement entries, which reduce to u_i v_i=0 (2 is invertible). The disjoint squarefree quadratic regular sequence proves reduced lci charts and all completed germ formulas for arbitrary n. Bipartition components and saturation follow from the global affine-chart cover; degrees follow by a verified Segre/Vandermonde count. Exact coefficient checks of all 1,16,100,400 3-minors for n=3..6 and formula checks n=3..11 supplement, but do not substitute for, the universal proof. The only unproved region is affine irrelevant-vertex behavior, explicitly outside the claim.

originality.rationale: The exact projective minor-scheme/local-germ classification is not supplied by the primary rank-two minimum-rank graph theorem of Grood et al. (2014), Theorem 2.3: it identifies complete-bipartite support graphs of real matrices but does not assert reduced ideals, saturated intersections, completed singularity types or local multiplicities. Bruns--Romer--Wiebe (2003) study generic rectangular determinantal rings, not a structural-zero symmetric linear section. Indexed related quartic determinantal singular-scheme findings do not imply the universal all-size hollow rank-two ideal theorem. Negative searches alone do not certify novelty; historical equivalence remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed complex-algebraic/symmetric-zero-diagonal determinantal treatment could contain an equivalent chart theorem.
The finite checker cannot certify an infinite result; the block-ideal equality and regular-sequence proof are the actual universal evidence.
No independent mathematical audit has been undertaken.

value.rationale: Determining whether a sparse symmetric rank-stratum linear section is scheme-theoretically reduced and the exact singularity type at its component intersections is a natural gap not answered by graph support classifications. The theorem gives every local completed ring for all n, a canonical product of independent node factors, a saturated ideal classification, branch multiplicity 2^z and Hilbert--Samuel series varying with zero-row strata. These are structural invariants of a natural infinite determinantal family with exponentially deep intersection multiplicities; the theorem does not claim unrelated downstream applications or novelty of the older support and aggregate-degree formulas.
